A_target.statement:
Let $X$ be a [[Definition:Compact Hausdorff Space|compact Hausdorff space]].
Then $X$ is [[Definition:Normal Space|normal]]: disjoint [[Definition:Closed Set (Topology)|closed sets]] $E$ and $F$ have disjoint open neighbourhoods.

B_source.statement:
Let $X$ be a [[Definition:Hausdorff Space|Hausdorff space]], $K \subseteq X$ [[Definition:Compact Subspace|compact]] and $x \notin K$.
Then there are disjoint open sets $U \ni x$ and $V \supseteq K$.

derived.finitely many point separations: a separation of two compact sets

object_map.reformulation: Separate each point of E from F, then use compactness of E to keep only finitely many separations.

validity_conditions: Closed subsets of a compact space are compact.
The intersection of the V's must be finite to remain open.
proof_plan: As $X$ is compact, the closed sets $E$ and $F$ are compact.
For each $x \in E$, the source result gives disjoint open $U_x \ni x$ and $V_x \supseteq F$.

By compactness of $E$, finitely many $U_{x_1}, \ldots, U_{x_n}$ cover $E$.
Let $U = \displaystyle \bigcup_i U_{x_i}$ and $V = \displaystyle \bigcap_i V_{x_i}$.
